headline: Three levels of wrapping is where per-level work becomes the whole measurement: the lanes that concatenate the chain during the build do not move at all, and every lane that merges at render time pays three times.

microbench.why: `next-yak-css-9.7` renders at 0.517 ms/1k, indistinguishable from its own depth-1 figure, because the css-prop fold concatenates the whole chain into one class on the plain element. `vanilla` at 0.509 is the floor and the fold ties it. Everything that merges per level climbs: `bamboo` 0.805 ms/1k running a `cx()` join at each level, `stylex-layers` 0.934 through `styleq`, `tailwind-merge` 1.31 running three merges, and `panda` 2.24 re-resolving each level's object for 1.28 ms of component self-time. The 9.6.0 runtime at 2.40 ms/1k is what one React component per level costs before the chain is flattened.

autocannon.why: `next-yak-css-9.7` 1,540 req/s and `vanilla` 1,530 against `next-yak-9.7`'s 1,190, the residual wrapper at the `styled(Component)` seam being the whole gap. `panda` collapses to 243 req/s, re-resolving three merged objects per element on every request, and the 9.6.0 runtime to 384.

attribution.why: `vanilla` (0.626 ms) and `next-yak-css-9.7` (0.632, with 0.256 ms of library time) are the floor. `panda` puts 1.28 of its 2.19 ms into component self-time and 34.4 ms of a 58.9 ms JS window inside its own package. `stylex-layers` shows the atomic merge directly, 0.222 ms of library slice plus 0.316 of component, and `tailwind-merge` 0.975 ms of library for three merge calls. The 9.6.0 runtime at 2.84 ms is the counter-example: 48.4 ms of runtime in the profile, three nested `Yak` components per instance.

hydrate.why: 48.1-54.6 ms of pure JS for the extracted and atomic lanes, no style and no layout inside the span. `styled-components` (103 ms) and `goober` (106 ms) inject and pay 0.22-0.23 ms of recalculation plus a layout pass. Spreads inside the fast cluster reach 49%, so treat its internal order as a tie.

inp.why: Re-rendering one three-level button costs under 0.7 ms of span JS in every lane and the field lands at 6.5-9.9 ms, one measurement wide. Depth reaches the server and the sweep but not a single interaction, since only one element's subtree re-renders.

mount.why: 73.7-92.4 ms for the lanes that mount a finished sheet. `emotion` (113 ms), `goober` (107) and `styled-components` (101) build theirs first, and `panda` at 89.8 ms carries a 9.19 ms layout against the cluster's 5.9-6.8 while it resolves.

renderTiming.why: One recalculation, one layout, two paints in every lane; counts tie. Composition changes how many class tokens an element carries, not how many times the browser has to recalculate, and the 0.129-0.190 ms spread of recalc cost bears that out.

payload.why: `next-yak-css-9.7` ships 2.66 kB gzipped, the same as at depth 1 and depth 6, because the whole chain folds into one numbered class. `vanilla` needs 3.04 kB to say the same thing by hand. `bamboo` (5.37 kB) and `panda` (8.31) carry one class token per level per element in the markup, and the utility lanes 14.1-15.1 kB of scanned sheet.

nsweep.why: `vanilla` (2.09 ms at n=4,000) and `next-yak-css-9.7` (2.11) are flat and linear. Every per-level mechanism multiplies by both depth and n: `bamboo` 3.16 ms, `stylex-layers` 3.82, `tailwind-merge` 5.30, `panda` 11.1 and the 9.6.0 runtime 9.81, the last two being the only shipped and diagnostic lanes whose line bends visibly.

crossCase: Bracketed by the Examples `compose-1` and `compose-6` shown nearby, this case shows how each mechanism scales with depth. `next-yak-css-9.7` reads 0.522, 0.517, 0.517 ms/1k across the three and its payload 2.67, 2.66, 2.66 kB: depth costs the css-prop fold nothing at all. `bamboo` climbs 0.553 to 0.805 to 1.13, `stylex-layers` 0.530 to 0.934 to 1.36, `panda` 1.18 to 2.24 to 3.47, and the 9.6.0 runtime 1.17 to 2.40 to 5.07 as it renders one component per level.
